## The name

An *emaki* (絵巻) is a Japanese picture handscroll: a long painted scene held
between two rolls, read by winding it from one to the other, a span at a
time. It is a good name for a window whose job is an agent chat too long to
see at once.

The app's icon is a handscroll seen from the front, with an agent chat on
its sheet: the agent on the left with its spark, your reply on the right.
This one carries a landscape instead, and winds as you move across it.

## Why it exists

Claude Code deletes its transcripts after `cleanupPeriodDays`, thirty by
default, with no warning. Every other tool in this space reads
`~/.claude/projects` and stops there, so they all inherit that expiry.

So Emaki copies first and renders second. The archive sweep runs before
anything else touches a session, for exactly this reason: if rendering
fails, the bytes are already safe. The archive is not a backup but a peer
source: live and kept transcripts are read together, so a session Claude
Code has deleted stays listed, searchable and readable, marked *kept*.

Compaction, for what it is worth, was never the threat: it appends a
boundary and keeps writing to the same file, leaving the earlier rows
intact.

## How it is built

Rust, with [GPUI](https://www.gpui.rs), the Zed editor's UI framework, and
[gpui-component](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-component) for the
window. There is no daemon, no browser and no hook.

```
crates/emaki-core   everything without a window, and the CLI
crates/emaki-app    the window
vendor/             gpui-component, with a few changes of ours
scripts/            packaging, the icon, the status line
```

The core works in this order:

1. **Adapters**, one per agent, find each agent's sessions on disk.
2. **Archive** copies Claude Code's byte for byte, before anything else
   touches them.
3. **Build** parses the JSONL transcript into a model of rounds, items and
   tool calls. The transcript is the only source of truth.
4. **Render** writes that model as markdown under `~/.emaki/logs`.
5. **Search** indexes every item in SQLite FTS5.

The app reads the same model and draws it. A file watcher says when to look
again. To reply, it writes to a terminal session's inbox, or runs a headless
agent of its own that appends to the same transcript.

## Where it is going

Three stages. The first is a complete app for Claude Code: permanent
history, organization by recency, project and agent, readable chats,
and an explanation on any step. The second is the public release and the
feedback that comes with it. The third extends the same to Codex, Kimi and
the other mainstream coding agents, so Emaki works across all of them.

Codex arrived in v0.2.0, ahead of its stage; the [releases](https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki/releases)
are the honest record of where things stand.

## Credits

The home page's figure follows the line-drawing manner of
[hairline](https://github.com/lucasmarkes/hairline)'s figures: nothing
filled, no words, what is far is dimmer, and one bright mark.

Icons are [Tabler](https://tabler.io/icons)'s outline set, drawn at a stroke
of 1.75 where Tabler's own is 2, in the app and on this site. The file
tree's icons are [Catppuccin](https://github.com/catppuccin/vscode-icons)'s.
The code colors are [Rosé Pine](https://rosepinetheme.com)'s hues, retinted
for contrast. The terminal keeps [Kaku](https://github.com/kakuapp)'s cream
in the light appearance. Every face the app carries is under the SIL Open
Font License, and so are this site's: Source Serif 4, JetBrains Mono and
Belleza. The site is made with [Quarto](https://quarto.org).
